h1: What to wear to a wedding as a guest
title: What to wear to a wedding as a guest · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a wedding? See three complete guest outfits for your time, weather and dress code, each with a real photo.
context: Wedding guest · Evening · 13°C · Formality 8 · Dressy
intro: For an evening wedding, aim for dressy but not formal: a polished outfit in a fabric that suits the season, with nothing that competes with the couple. When in doubt, choose something that looks finished from head to toe and avoid white, ivory and anything that looks like bridal wear. The example here is an evening wedding at 13°C, which calls for a substantial fabric or a layer you can keep on.

looks.caption: Navy pleated sheath dress, black pointed pumps, a gold bracelet.
looks.why: The Classic look works because a navy pleated sheath dress is a reliable wedding choice: the color is elegant, the silhouette is clean, and black pointed pumps and a gold bracelet add polish without distraction.

looks.caption: Colour-blocked satin gown in green, red and blue, a pink and yellow head wrap.
looks.why: The Bold look works for guests who want to stand out a little. A colour-blocked satin gown in green, red and blue makes a statement, and a pink and yellow head wrap adds personality, as long as the rest of the outfit stays simple.

looks.caption: Cream short-sleeve blazer, wide-leg trousers, pointed heels.
looks.why: The Relaxed look works when you want comfort with a sharp edge. A cream short-sleeve blazer over wide-leg trousers with pointed heels reads as put-together and dressy, and the blazer gives you something to layer when the evening cools.

tips: Check the invitation for dress code cues like 'black tie optional' or 'cocktail,' and if the couple has a seasonal theme, follow it lightly.
At 13°C, bring a layer such as a wrap, blazer or light coat, since outdoor photos and evening air can feel cold even when the day was mild.
Choose closed-toe or dressy shoes you can stand in for hours; if the venue is a lawn or gravel, pick a block heel or flat dressy shoe.
Keep the palette to two or three main colors so bold pieces look intentional; deep jewel tones, navy, cream and metallics all work well.
Finish with simple details like a clutch, a watch or one statement earring, and keep hair and makeup polished but not overly formal.
avoid: White, ivory or cream full looks that could be mistaken for the bride's outfit.
Casual items such as denim, sneakers, graphic tees or flip-flops, even if the venue feels relaxed.
Anything so revealing or so sheer that it needs constant adjusting during the ceremony and dinner.

faq.q: What should a man wear to an evening wedding as a guest?
faq.a: A suit in navy or charcoal with a dress shirt and tie is the safest choice for a dressy evening wedding. A cream or light grey suit can work for a summer or daytime event, and a dark overcoat or topcoat covers the cool evening air well.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear black to a wedding?
faq.a: Black is acceptable at most evening weddings, especially when dressed up with color or texture in accessories. Some couples ask guests to avoid black for daytime or casual events, so check the invitation or wedding website if you're unsure.

faq.q: How do I dress for an outdoor wedding without ruining my outfit?
faq.a: Choose block heels or flat dressy shoes for grass and gravel, and bring a light layer for temperature changes. Fabrics that resist wrinkling and avoid trailing hems will keep you comfortable and presentable through the day.

h1: What to wear to an art gallery opening
title: What to wear to an art gallery opening · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a gallery opening? See three complete outfits for the evening, from polished to relaxed, built for the weather.
context: Gallery opening · Evening · 17°C · Formality 6 · Business casual
intro: For an art gallery opening, aim for smart business casual: put-together and a little considered, but never formal. Dress for an evening that is likely to be on your feet, indoors and mingling, with the art as the focus rather than your outfit. Pieces that look sharp, move comfortably, and suit a room that may be warm or cool are the safest bet.

looks.caption: Olive suit over a matching turtleneck, black leather oxfords.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs an olive suit with a matching turtleneck and black leather oxfords. The tonal palette looks deliberate and polished, and the knit keeps the look relaxed enough for a crowded opening.

looks.caption: Emerald car coat, wide blue trousers, burgundy loafers, a grey slouch bag.
looks.why: The Bold look combines an emerald car coat, wide blue trousers, burgundy loafers and a grey slouch bag. The jewel-tone coat makes a statement while the grey bag and neutral trousers keep the color balanced.

looks.caption: Light-blue linen shirt with rolled sleeves, grey chinos, suede lace-ups.
looks.why: The Relaxed look is a light-blue linen shirt with rolled sleeves, grey chinos and suede lace-ups. It feels effortless and easy to move in, and it reads as thoughtful rather than casual when the shoes and shirt are well chosen.

tips: Choose business casual as your baseline: tailored pieces, no sportswear, no formal wear unless the invite says black tie.
Check the evening temperature and bring a layer you can carry, like a coat or knit, since gallery rooms can run cool and crowded rooms run warm.
Wear shoes you can stand in for two hours. Leather oxfords, loafers and suede lace-ups all work well; avoid new shoes.
Keep colors coordinated: one or two strong colors plus neutrals like grey, navy, cream or black, so the art stays the focus.
Pay attention to details like a clean bag, neat hemlines and a simple watch or jewelry, rather than adding more pieces.
avoid: Heavy logos or loud graphic prints that compete with the artwork on the walls.
Very casual items such as gym shoes, shorts or worn-out denim if the invite suggests dressing up.
Bulky bags or oversized coats you will have to carry through crowded rooms.

faq.q: What is the dress code for an art gallery opening?
faq.a: Business casual is the usual dress code: smart, put-together clothes without a formal suit and tie or cocktail dress. If the invitation says black tie or cocktail, follow that instead.

faq.q: Can I wear jeans to a gallery opening?
faq.a: Yes, if they are dark, well-fitted and paired with a sharper top and shoes, such as a knit or blazer with leather loafers. Avoid distressed or faded jeans with sneakers unless the event is clearly casual.

faq.q: What should women wear to an art gallery opening?
faq.a: Tailored trousers, a midi skirt, or a simple dress with a structured layer like a blazer or coat all work well. Choose comfortable heels or flats since you will be standing and walking for a while.

h1: Casual weekend outfits for time with friends
title: Casual weekend outfits for time with friends · Peppi
description: Casual weekend outfits for time with friends: what to wear, how to layer for the weather, and three complete looks to see on Peppi.
context: Weekend with friends · Afternoon · 15°C · Formality 3 · Casual
intro: For time with friends on a casual weekend, aim for comfortable clothes that still look put together. Relaxed fabrics, a layer you can take off, and shoes you can walk in will cover almost any plan. Pick one piece that feels a little more considered, and the rest can stay easy.

looks.caption: Charcoal zip knit over a grey collared shirt, dark indigo jeans, dark sneakers.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a charcoal zip knit over a grey collared shirt with dark indigo jeans and dark sneakers. It is neat without feeling formal, and the zip knit gives you an easy layer for a cool afternoon.

looks.caption: Mustard top, a multicolour striped midi skirt, white sneakers.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a mustard top with a multicolour striped midi skirt and white sneakers. The warm color and pattern make it stand out, while the clean white shoes keep it relaxed and wearable all day.

looks.caption: White crew-neck tee, light relaxed jeans, cream slides.
looks.why: The Relaxed look is a white crew-neck tee with light relaxed jeans and cream slides. It is the easiest option for a long, unplanned afternoon, and the soft neutrals look fresh rather than careless.

tips: Dress for the casual end of the scale: well-fitting basics beat anything that needs careful handling.
At 15°C, layer rather than bundle. A knit, overshirt or light jacket is easy to remove once you warm up in a café or in the sun.
Choose shoes for walking first. Sneakers or clean flat sandals work for most weekend plans, and slides suit warmer, more relaxed days.
Keep your palette to two or three colors, such as neutrals with one accent like mustard, so the outfit looks intentional.
Check the details: hems at the right length, collars that lie flat, and clean shoes. Small finishing touches make casual clothes look deliberate.
avoid: Stiff formal pieces like dress shoes or structured blazers, which feel out of place with friends.
Anything you will need to adjust constantly, such as very long skirts or wide sleeves that get in the way.
Heavy outerwear you will have to carry all afternoon when a light layer would do.

faq.q: What is a good casual weekend outfit for women?
faq.a: A midi skirt or relaxed jeans with a knit or a crew-neck tee works well, finished with sneakers or flat sandals. Add a light layer for cooler moments. Women and men can use the same logic: comfortable fit, one accent piece, and shoes you can walk in.

faq.q: What should men wear for a casual weekend with friends?
faq.a: Relaxed jeans or chinos with a crew-neck tee, a collared shirt, or a zip knit works well. Clean sneakers or slides finish the look. A light layer you can take off keeps you comfortable as the day changes.

faq.q: What do you wear to hang out outside when it is cool?
faq.a: Layer a knit or lightweight jacket over a simple base, and choose closed shoes if you will be walking. At around 15°C, a single extra layer you can remove is usually better than one heavy coat.

h1: What to wear for a day in the city
title: What to wear for a day in the city · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear for a day in the city? See three complete outfits, checked against the weather, from classic to relaxed.
context: City day out · Morning · 9°C · Formality 4 · Casual chic
intro: For a day in the city, aim for casual chic: polished enough for a café or a gallery, comfortable enough to walk for hours. Choose one structured layer, shoes you can walk in, and a palette of two or three colors. Peppi checks the weather where you'll be and builds outfits around it, so you can start from a look that already works.

looks.caption: Stone trench coat over a navy knit dress, knee-high black boots.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a stone trench coat with a navy knit dress and knee-high black boots. The neutral palette and tailored coat keep it sharp, and the boots add structure without sacrificing comfort.

looks.caption: Red blanket coat with a black stripe, dark jeans, navy trainers.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a red blanket coat with a black stripe over dark jeans and navy trainers. The coat carries the outfit, and the trainers keep it practical for a full day of walking.

looks.caption: Patterned overshirt over a check shirt, grey wide trousers, black loafers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look layers a patterned overshirt over a check shirt, with grey wide trousers and black loafers. Mixed prints feel effortless when the base colors stay muted, and loafers look dressed up without being fussy.

tips: Dress for the dress code: casual chic means nice fabrics and clean fit, not formal wear or gym clothes.
At 9°C in the morning, layer. A coat or overshirt you can open or take off covers the temperature swing before noon.
Wear shoes you've already walked in. City days often mean 10,000 steps, so break in boots or trainers before the day.
Limit your palette to two or three colors, or one bold color plus neutrals, so the outfit looks deliberate.
Keep the details tidy: a belt that matches your shoes, a bag that fits your daily essentials, and no items you'll need to adjust all day.
avoid: Heels or stiff leather soles you can't walk comfortably in for hours.
A single thin layer when the morning is cold; you'll be uncomfortable by midday or caught out by the wind.
Too many competing prints or logos, which looks busy rather than styled.

faq.q: What should I wear for a day in the city in cold weather?
faq.a: Layer a structured outer piece, like a trench or wool coat, over a knit or shirt, and wear closed shoes with good grip. Choose items you can open or remove as the day warms up.

faq.q: Is jeans okay for a city day out?
faq.a: Yes, as long as they're dark, well-fitted, and paired with a polished top or outer layer. Add shoes that look neat, such as clean trainers or loafers, to keep the look casual chic.

faq.q: What shoes are best for walking around the city all day?
faq.a: Choose comfortable shoes with cushioning and a flexible sole, such as clean trainers, loafers with a rubber sole, or boots you've already broken in. Avoid anything you haven't walked in before.

h1: What to wear to dinner with friends
title: What to wear to dinner with friends · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to dinner with friends? See three complete smart-casual outfits, checked against the weather, and pick your favorite.
context: Dinner with friends · Evening · 8°C · Formality 5 · Smart casual
intro: For dinner with friends, smart casual is the safe target: polished enough to feel like you made an effort, relaxed enough that nobody feels overdressed. Aim for well-fitting clothes, one clean layer, and shoes you'd be happy to sit in for two hours. The example below is for an evening at 8°C with a formality level of 5 out of 10.

looks.caption: Camel overcoat, black scarf, grey knit, brown leather boots.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a camel overcoat with a grey knit and black trousers, finished with a black scarf and brown leather boots. It reads warm and put-together, and the coat handles the chill on the walk over.

looks.caption: Brown corduroy blazer, a paisley tie, mint wide-leg trousers.
looks.why: The Bold look brings in a brown corduroy blazer, a paisley tie and mint wide-leg trousers. Pick it when you want a little personality; the tie is the one piece to keep patterned, so the rest of the outfit stays calm.

looks.caption: Black denim jacket over a grey hoodie, grey trousers, chunky sneakers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look layers a black denim jacket over a grey hoodie with grey trousers and chunky sneakers. It's the most casual of the three and works well for a laid-back restaurant or a friend's home.

tips: Dress to the place, not the invitation: a casual bistro suits the Relaxed look, while a white-tablecloth spot calls for the Classic.
Layer for the temperature: at 8°C, a coat or jacket you can leave on the chair matters more than a heavy sweater.
Choose shoes you can walk and sit in comfortably; leather boots or clean sneakers beat anything you'll be adjusting all night.
Keep the palette to two or three colors so the outfit looks intentional. Neutrals like grey, black and camel are easy to combine.
Let one detail do the talking, such as a scarf, a tie, or a bold watch, and keep the rest simple.
avoid: Heavy athletic gear or worn-out sneakers, which can read as not trying at all.
Too many competing patterns or logos in one outfit.
Anything you have to keep fixing, like a scarf that slips or shoes that pinch.

faq.q: What is smart casual for dinner with friends?
faq.a: Smart casual means clean, well-fitting clothes that look intentional without being formal. A knit, tailored trousers or dark jeans, and a jacket or coat usually hit the mark. Skip suits unless the group has said it's a dressy occasion.

faq.q: What should I wear to dinner with friends in cold weather?
faq.a: Wear a base layer you're comfortable in, a sweater or knit, and an outer layer like a coat or denim jacket. Choose something easy to take off indoors, since restaurants can get warm once everyone arrives.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear jeans to dinner with friends?
faq.a: Yes, as long as they're dark, well-fitted and in good condition. Pair them with a blazer, a knit or a clean button-down so they don't look like everyday wear.

h1: What to wear to birthday drinks
title: What to wear to birthday drinks · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to birthday drinks? See three smart-casual outfits built for an evening out, with the right layers and shoes.
context: Birthday drinks · Evening · 20°C · Formality 5 · Smart casual
intro: For birthday drinks in the evening, smart casual is the safest choice: polished enough to feel celebratory, relaxed enough to move around a bar or restaurant. Aim for one good piece, such as a blazer or a striking top, paired with comfortable, well-fitting bottoms and shoes you can stand in for a few hours.

looks.caption: Black blazer, blush blouse, slim black trousers, white sneakers.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a black blazer and slim black trousers with a blush blouse, so it reads polished without being formal. White sneakers keep it current and comfortable for drinks that run late.

looks.caption: Black blazer and bodysuit, red tights, strappy black heels.
looks.why: The Bold look builds around a black blazer and bodysuit, with red tights and strappy black heels adding color and a bit of celebration. It suits a crowd that is dressing up and works well for a birthday where you want to stand out.

looks.caption: Oversized brown tee, a gold necklace, flared jeans, white sneakers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look uses an oversized brown tee, flared jeans and white sneakers, with a gold necklace to lift the outfit. It is the easiest choice when the invitation is casual and you want to feel comfortable all night.

tips: Treat smart casual as your baseline: one dressed-up element plus one relaxed element keeps you from looking overdressed.
Evening temperatures often drop after dark, so bring a layer like a blazer, cardigan or light jacket you can take on and off.
Choose shoes you can stand in for hours; sneakers and block heels both work for drinks, while very high heels are harder to keep up with.
Pick one accent color, such as blush or red, and keep the rest of the outfit in neutrals like black, white or brown for a clean look.
Add one statement detail, like a gold necklace, a bold earring or colored tights, rather than layering several competing accessories.
avoid: Avoid wearing a full suit or cocktail dress unless the invitation specifically asks for dressy, since it can feel out of place at a casual gathering.
Avoid heavily scented perfume or cologne, which can be overwhelming in a small, crowded space.
Avoid stiff, new shoes you have not walked in; blisters can end a fun night early.

faq.q: What is the dress code for birthday drinks?
faq.a: Birthday drinks are usually smart casual, meaning you dress nicer than everyday clothes but not formally. Unless the invite says otherwise, a blazer or nice top with clean trousers or jeans is a safe middle ground.

faq.q: Should I dress up more for a birthday drinks party?
faq.a: A little more than usual is a good idea, since it is a celebration. Adding one polished piece, like a blazer or a bold top, shows you made an effort without making the group feel underdressed or overdressed.

faq.q: Can I wear sneakers to birthday drinks?
faq.a: Yes, clean white or minimal sneakers work well for smart-casual drinks, especially paired with trousers or flared jeans. For a dressier feel, choose a sleek leather pair and avoid worn-out or athletic styles.

h1: What to wear on a school trip
title: What to wear on a school trip · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear on a school trip? Get three complete outfit ideas for the weather and your plans, each with a real photo, on Peppi.
context: School trip · Morning · 16°C · Formality 2 · Very casual
intro: For a school trip, dress for comfort first: you'll likely be walking, sitting on a bus, and possibly standing around outdoors. Choose relaxed, easy-to-move clothes with a layer you can add or remove, and shoes you can walk in all day. Peppi builds outfits around the weather at your destination and how casual you want to be.

looks.caption: Green cropped tee, straight light-wash jeans, canvas sneakers.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a green cropped tee with straight light-wash jeans and canvas sneakers. It's clean, neat, and easy to walk in, so it works well for a museum or a day of sightseeing.

looks.caption: Teal denim overalls, a striped tee, black skate shoes.
looks.why: The Bold look uses teal denim overalls over a striped tee, with black skate shoes. The bright color and playful stripes make it stand out, and the sturdy shoes handle long walks.

looks.caption: White V-neck tee, light skinny jeans, black sneakers, a backpack.
looks.why: The Relaxed look is a white V-neck tee with light skinny jeans, black sneakers, and a backpack. It's the most low-effort option and keeps your hands free, which helps on busy days.

tips: Check the forecast for the destination, not just your home town, since temperatures can differ a lot, especially for a morning start.
Wear layers: a tee under a light jacket, hoodie, or overshirt lets you adjust on a cool bus or a warm afternoon.
Break in your shoes before the trip. Sneakers or skate shoes with good support matter more than any other piece.
Choose jeans or pants that move well. Straight or relaxed cuts are comfortable for sitting and walking; very tight fits can feel restrictive after hours on your feet.
Keep colors simple with one brighter piece, such as a green or teal top, and neutrals like white, black, or denim for everything else. Pieces that mix easily make packing simpler.
avoid: Brand-new shoes you haven't walked in, since blisters can ruin a day out.
Heavy bags or big purses that dig into your shoulder; a small backpack distributes weight better.
Overly dressy or delicate clothes, like satin or white fabrics that show dirt, when you'll be on buses, grass, or crowded spaces.

faq.q: What should I wear on a school trip in cold weather?
faq.a: Layer a warm base tee or long-sleeve top under a fleece, hoodie, or light jacket. Jeans or sturdy pants and closed-toe sneakers keep you comfortable. Bring a layer you can take off indoors or when it warms up.

faq.q: Are jeans okay for a school trip?
faq.a: Yes, jeans are a practical choice for most school trips. Pick a comfortable, straight or relaxed cut that you can walk and sit in easily, and avoid very stiff or tight denim.

faq.q: What shoes are best for a school trip?
faq.a: Comfortable, supportive sneakers are the best choice because you'll likely walk a lot. Pick a pair you've already worn in, with good grip for outdoor paths and buses.

h1: What to wear to a family lunch
title: What to wear to a family lunch · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a family lunch? See three complete outfits, Classic, Bold and Relaxed, picked for the weather and how dressed up you want to be.
context: Family lunch · Midday · 14°C · Formality 4 · Casual chic
intro: For a family lunch, aim for casual chic: put together and comfortable, a step above what you'd wear to run errands. A neat top, trousers or a skirt, and shoes you can sit in all afternoon is a safe choice that suits most families. Start with the weather and the time of day, then choose how polished you want to look.

looks.caption: Black cardigan over a white shirt, khaki trousers, brown leather shoes.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a black cardigan over a white shirt with khaki trousers and brown leather shoes. It's tidy, easy to dress up or down, and the cardigan lets you adjust if the room is warm or cool.

looks.caption: Red and grey striped peplum top with a matching maxi skirt, strappy sandals.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a red and grey striped peplum top with a matching maxi skirt and strappy sandals. The coordinated stripes make it feel intentional and festive without being fussy, and it suits a warm midday lunch.

looks.caption: Oatmeal hoodie, wide camel trousers, a quilted crossbody bag.
looks.why: The Relaxed look combines an oatmeal hoodie, wide camel trousers and a quilted crossbody bag. It's the most comfortable option for long meals and kid-friendly settings, and it still looks considered rather than sloppy.

tips: Match the dress code to the host: if it's a home lunch, go one step more polished than you'd wear to a casual brunch with friends.
At around 14°C, dress in layers: a cardigan, jacket or light knit you can take off once you're inside or in the sun.
Choose shoes you can walk and sit in comfortably; leather loafers, low heels or clean sneakers all work, depending on the look.
Stick to two or three colors, such as neutrals with one accent shade, so the outfit looks put together.
Keep details simple: a watch, small earrings or a belt are enough, and avoid anything that will get in the way at the table.
avoid: Heavy or overly formal outfits like a suit or cocktail dress, which can feel out of place at a relaxed family meal.
Very tight or revealing clothes, since you'll be sitting, bending and reaching for dishes all afternoon.
Brand-new shoes or outfits you haven't worn before, in case they rub or feel uncomfortable by dessert.

faq.q: What is the best outfit for a family lunch?
faq.a: A smart-casual outfit is usually safest: neat trousers or a skirt with a clean top and a layer you can remove. The Classic look, a cardigan over a white shirt with khaki trousers, is a reliable choice for most families.

faq.q: Is jeans okay for a family lunch?
faq.a: Yes, if they're dark, well-fitted and paired with a nicer top and shoes. Avoid distressed or faded pairs unless the lunch is very casual or outdoors. For a more polished look, trousers or a midi skirt work better.

faq.q: What should a man wear to a family lunch?
faq.a: Chinos or dark trousers with a button-down or fine knit, and loafers or clean leather shoes, works well. Add a light jacket or cardigan for cooler weather, and skip a tie unless the family is especially formal.

h1: What to wear to a job interview
title: What to wear to a job interview · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a job interview? Get three complete outfit ideas matched to the weather and dress code. See the looks on Peppi.
context: Job interview · Morning · 18°C · Formality 8 · Business formal
intro: For most job interviews, wear business formal: a well-fitted suit or a tailored blazer with matching trousers, in a neutral or dark color. Choose clothes that are a step more polished than the job's everyday dress, since that shows you took the meeting seriously. Make sure everything fits well and is clean and pressed.

looks.caption: Camel wide-leg trouser suit, a black blouse, burgundy pumps.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a camel wide-leg trouser suit with a black blouse and burgundy pumps. The neutral suit reads as professional, and the burgundy shoes add a touch of personality without distracting.

looks.caption: Bright red suit, a white shirt and patterned tie, brown derbies.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a bright red suit with a white shirt and patterned tie, finished with brown derbies. It's a confident choice for creative fields or interviews where you want to be memorable, but keep the rest of the outfit simple so the suit does the talking.

looks.caption: Black blazer and turtleneck, slim black trousers, nude pumps.
looks.why: The Relaxed look combines a black blazer and turtleneck with slim black trousers and nude pumps. It feels modern and understated, and works well for tech, design, or startup interviews where a stiff suit might feel out of place.

tips: Check the company's website or social media, or ask the recruiter, to gauge the dress code, then go one level more formal.
At 18°C, a blazer or light coat is usually enough. Bring a layer you can take off, since offices are often warm or cold in unexpected ways.
Wear closed-toe shoes that are polished or clean. Shoes are one of the first things people notice, so keep them in good condition.
Stick to two or three colors. Neutrals like black, navy, gray, camel, or white are safe, with one accent color if you want some personality.
Keep accessories minimal: a simple watch, small earrings or cufflinks, and one ring at most. Make sure any hair, nails, and bags look neat.
avoid: Jeans, sneakers, graphic tees, or anything wrinkled, stained, or too casual for the role.
Strong perfume or cologne, since interviewers may be sensitive to scent in a small room.
Clothes that are too tight, too short, too loose, or that you have to adjust during the conversation.

faq.q: What should I wear to a job interview if the company is casual?
faq.a: Dress one step above the company's everyday style. Smart separates, like tailored trousers or a skirt with a clean blouse or knit and a blazer, usually work well. You can skip the full suit while still looking intentional.

faq.q: Can I wear a suit to a virtual job interview?
faq.a: Yes, and it's a good idea to dress as you would in person. Wear the top half you'll see on camera in a solid color, avoid busy patterns that can blur on video, and check your lighting and background beforehand.

faq.q: Should my interview outfit be different for men and women?
faq.a: The principles are the same for everyone: good fit, neutral colors, and polished shoes. Men often wear a suit with a tie or open collar, while women have more options with blouses, dresses, or trouser suits, but both should look professional and comfortable.

h1: Date night outfit ideas
title: Date night outfit ideas · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear on a date? See three complete smart-casual outfits matched to the weather and your plans. Try them on Peppi.
context: Date night · Evening · 19°C · Formality 6 · Smart casual
intro: For a date night, smart casual is the safest target: dressed up enough to look like you made an effort, relaxed enough to feel like yourself. At around 19°C in the evening, a shirt or top with trousers or dark jeans and one layer you can take off works for almost anyone. Peppi builds three complete outfits for your exact evening, so you can pick the one that fits your mood.

looks.caption: Black shirt, black tailored trousers, brown leather loafers.
looks.why: Classic: a black shirt, black tailored trousers and brown leather loafers. Clean, sharp and hard to get wrong, and the tailoring makes it look intentional.

looks.caption: Burgundy off-shoulder top and wide trousers, a satin coat over the shoulders.
looks.why: Bold: a burgundy off-shoulder top with wide trousers, and a satin coat draped over the shoulders for the evening. It stands out without being loud, and the coat gives you something to take off or put back on.

looks.caption: Navy short-sleeve shirt, dark jeans, a mustard jacket over one shoulder.
looks.why: Relaxed: a navy short-sleeve shirt with dark jeans and a mustard jacket worn over one shoulder. Easy to move in, and the mustard adds warmth and personality to a simple base.

tips: Aim for one step above what you'd wear to a casual day out, and match the level of the place you're going: a bar and a bistro are different dress codes.
At about 19°C, bring one layer you can add or remove, like a jacket, overshirt or light coat. Evenings cool off faster than you expect once you're outside.
Choose shoes that are comfortable for walking and standing. Leather loafers, boots or clean minimal sneakers all work, depending on how dressy the night is.
Stick to two or three colors. One bold piece, like burgundy or mustard, looks deliberate; several competing colors can look busy.
Pay attention to fit at the shoulders and hem. A slightly tailored fit does more for a date look than any single statement piece.
avoid: Wearing anything you haven't worn before without trying it on first; comfort shows in how you move and sit.
Overdressing to a casual spot, which can make the evening feel more formal than you intended.
Strong fragrance and heavily branded clothing, which can be distracting in a close setting.

faq.q: What should I wear on a first date?
faq.a: Choose something smart casual that you feel confident in: well-fitted trousers or dark jeans with a shirt, knit or blouse, and comfortable shoes. Aim to look put together without looking like you're going to an interview.

faq.q: How dressy should a date night outfit be?
faq.a: One step above your everyday look is usually right. Match the venue: a casual restaurant suits clean jeans and a nice top or shirt, while a formal dinner calls for tailored pieces and dressier shoes.

faq.q: What do I wear on a date when it's cold outside?
faq.a: Layer. A shirt or fitted top under a jacket, coat or knit lets you stay warm outdoors and comfortable indoors. Choose a layer that looks good on its own when you take it off.

h1: Beach vacation outfits
title: Beach vacation outfits · Peppi
description: Beach vacation outfits that work in the afternoon heat. See three complete looks, picked for your weather and how dressed up you want to be.
context: Beach holiday · Afternoon · 28°C · Formality 2 · Very casual
intro: For a beach vacation, aim for light, breathable clothes that are easy to throw on over swimwear and stay comfortable in the heat. Keep the look relaxed but put together, with one or two pieces that make it feel like a day out rather than the gym. When in doubt, choose loose fabrics, neutral or airy colors, and shoes you can walk sand in.

looks.caption: Flowing white sundress, a straw boater, a round woven bag, tan sandals.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a flowing white sundress with a straw boater, a round woven bag and tan sandals. White and natural tones reflect heat, the flowy cut lets air move, and the woven accessories suit the setting without looking like a costume.

looks.caption: Pastel tie-dye tee, black jeans, a black bucket hat.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a pastel tie-dye tee with black jeans and a black bucket hat. The bright print carries the vacation mood, while black jeans and a black hat ground it and give you a sun-shielding brim for the afternoon.

looks.caption: White broderie mini dress, mint sneakers, sunglasses.
looks.why: The Relaxed look is a white broderie mini dress with mint sneakers and sunglasses. Eyelet cotton is light and breezy, and the sneakers keep it comfortable for walking boardwalks and sandy paths, with sunglasses doing the real work for glare.

tips: Match the dress code to the spot: a beach town dinner calls for something a step up from a day at the sand.
Bring a light layer like an overshirt or linen wrap for air-conditioned restaurants and breezy evenings.
Choose sandals or canvas sneakers you can rinse off; leather and suede don't handle salt water well.
Stick to a palette of whites, creams, pastels or one bold print, and keep the rest neutral so pieces mix easily across days.
Protect yourself with a hat, sunglasses and a bag that holds sunscreen, water and a towel without weighing you down.
avoid: Heavy, stiff fabrics like thick denim or heavy knits, which trap heat and dry slowly after a swim.
Shoes with thin soles or delicate straps that sink into sand or slip on wet stone.
Too many dark colors in direct sun, which absorb heat and can feel stifling by mid-afternoon.

faq.q: What should I wear to the beach on vacation?
faq.a: Loose cotton, linen or light synthetic shorts or dresses, a breathable top, and sandals or sneakers you can get sandy. Add a hat and sunglasses and a cover-up for walking away from the water.

faq.q: What do I wear to dinner after a beach day?
faq.a: Swap the swim cover-up for a clean linen shirt, a midi or mini dress, or chinos with a tee. Keep the same easy shoes or switch to flat leather sandals if the restaurant is nicer.

faq.q: What should men wear on a beach vacation?
faq.a: Lightweight shorts or linen pants, a short-sleeve shirt or tee, and sandals or canvas sneakers. A bucket hat or cap and sunglasses finish the look, and a lightweight overshirt covers evenings.

h1: Business casual outfits for the office
title: Business casual outfits for the office · Peppi
description: Wondering what to wear to the office? See three business casual outfits for a 12°C morning, styled for your dress code, with real photos.
context: Office day · Morning · 12°C · Formality 6 · Business casual
intro: Business casual means polished but not formal: pieces that look intentional, fit well, and let you move comfortably through a workday. The safest approach is to choose tailored basics in neutral colors and add one considered detail, so you look put together whether the office is relaxed or more traditional.

looks.caption: Black crew-neck knit, black tailored trousers, black oxfords.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a black crew-neck knit with black tailored trousers and black oxfords. It is the lowest-risk option for an office with a traditional streak, and the matching tones make the outfit look sharp and deliberate.

looks.caption: Cream turtleneck, a rust and blush pleated midi skirt, tan heels.
looks.why: The Bold look uses a cream turtleneck with a rust and blush pleated midi skirt and tan heels. The warm palette adds personality without strain, and the pleats and turtleneck keep it refined enough for client meetings.

looks.caption: Light-blue linen suit, an open-collar white shirt, brown loafers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look combines a light-blue linen suit with an open-collar white shirt and brown loafers. It suits offices where a full suit feels heavy; the unstructured linen and open collar signal ease while the matching set keeps it professional.

tips: Read the dress code first: if your office is casual, the Relaxed look is often enough; if clients visit often, lean toward the Classic.
At 12°C in the morning, layer rather than bulk up. A knit, a blazer, or a light coat you can take off indoors works better than one heavy piece.
Choose shoes you can walk in all day. Oxfords, loafers, and low heels look professional without making you uncomfortable by afternoon.
Keep your palette to two or three colors. Neutrals like black, cream, tan, and navy are easy to mix and make the outfit look planned.
Pay attention to fit at the shoulders and hem, and choose a simple watch or small jewelry as the one detail that finishes the look.
avoid: Athletic wear, distressed denim, and graphic tees, which read as too casual for most offices.
Wrinkled or ill-fitting clothes; a well-pressed basic beats an expensive piece that does not fit.
Too many competing patterns or loud logos, which pull attention away from your work.

faq.q: What is business casual for the office?
faq.a: Business casual sits between formal business attire and weekend clothes. Think tailored trousers or skirts, knits, collared shirts, blazers, and closed-toe shoes, in clean, neutral colors that fit well.

faq.q: Can men wear business casual without a suit jacket?
faq.a: Yes. A collared shirt or fine knit with tailored chinos or trousers and leather shoes or loafers is standard business casual. Add a blazer when you want a more formal presence or meet clients.

faq.q: What should I wear to the office when it is cold?
faq.a: Layer lightweight pieces such as a fine knit, a shirt under a sweater or blazer, and a coat you can remove at your desk. Keep the layers in the same color family so the outfit still looks cohesive.

h1: What to wear to the theater

context: Theatre night · Evening · 11°C · Formality 7 · Dressy
intro: For the theater, aim for smart and polished: dressy, not formal. Think tailored pieces and good shoes rather than anything costume-like. When in doubt, choose one sharp focal point, such as a rich color or a statement texture, and keep everything else clean and simple.

looks.caption: Champagne sequin wrap dress, black heeled sandals, a silver bangle.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a champagne sequin wrap dress with black heeled sandals and a silver bangle. The sequins catch the house lights without being loud, and the wrap shape flatters on any body and sits comfortably through a long intermission.

looks.caption: Burgundy double-breasted suit, a blue patterned tie, tan shoes.
looks.why: The Bold look is a burgundy double-breasted suit with a blue patterned tie and tan shoes. It reads as deliberate and confident, and the tan shoes keep the rich color from feeling heavy.

looks.caption: White blazer over a lilac bodice, pale-blue satin wide trousers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look combines a white blazer over a lilac bodice with pale-blue satin wide trousers. It feels fresh and easy while still looking planned, and it works well for a casual-leaning theater crowd.

tips: Match the production: a formal opera or gala calls for more polish than a fringe or musical matinee.
At 11°C, bring a layer you can take off and carry, like a blazer, wrap, or light coat, since theater lobbies and seats can run warm or cold.
Choose shoes you can stand and sit in for two to three hours. Heeled sandals, loafers, and low block heels all work well.
Pick one strong color or texture and balance it with neutrals such as black, white, camel, or navy.
Keep accessories intentional and quiet: one bangle, a simple watch, or a single tie is enough so nothing clatters or distracts during a quiet scene.
avoid: Overly casual pieces like sneakers, gym wear, or distressed denim unless the show is a deliberately casual event.
Very bulky coats or large bags that block the view of people behind you.
Loud, jangling jewelry or sequins with nothing else going on, which can look like too much in a dark auditorium.

faq.q: What is the dress code for the theater?
faq.a: Most theaters have no strict dress code, but smart or dressy casual is the safe default. Dark or formal productions, opening nights, and galas usually call for more polish, such as a dress, suit, or tailored separates.

faq.q: Can men wear jeans to the theater?
faq.a: Dark, well-fitted jeans can work for a casual matinee or a fringe show, but pair them with a blazer or knit and clean shoes. For evening performances or larger venues, trousers or a suit will feel more appropriate.

faq.q: What should I wear to the theater when it is cold outside?
faq.a: Dress in layers you can remove easily, such as a fine-knit sweater, shirt, or dress under a blazer or wrap coat. Choose a coat that folds small so you can keep it on your lap or hang it on the seat.

h1: What to wear to a garden party
title: What to wear to a garden party · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a garden party? See three complete outfits matched to the weather, time and dress code. Get your look on Peppi.
context: Garden party · Afternoon · 24°C · Formality 5 · Smart casual
intro: For a garden party in the afternoon, aim for smart casual: polished enough to look intentional, light enough to stay comfortable in the sun. Breathable fabrics, a little color and sun protection will serve you better than anything formal or heavy.

looks.caption: White floral maxi dress, a straw sun hat, sunglasses.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a white floral maxi dress with a straw sun hat and sunglasses. It is the safest choice for most garden parties: it reads as dressed up without trying too hard, and the hat and sunglasses handle the afternoon sun.

looks.caption: Teal suit over a pink linen shirt, braces, a panama hat.
looks.why: The Bold look puts a teal suit over a pink linen shirt, finished with braces and a panama hat. The bright color and playful details suit a party where guests expect some personality, and the linen keeps it breathable.

looks.caption: White embroidered slip dress, a straw hat in hand, black flats.
looks.why: The Relaxed look is a white embroidered slip dress with a straw hat carried in hand and black flats. It keeps the outfit light and easy for a long afternoon on the lawn, and the black shoes add a grounding contrast.

tips: Read the invitation: a 'garden party' usually means smart casual, but a note like 'black tie optional' or 'cocktail attire' changes everything.
Choose breathable fabrics such as linen, cotton, or lightweight blends, especially above about 20°C.
Bring a layer for when the sun drops. A light cardigan, jacket, or wrap is easy to carry and useful in the evening.
Wear shoes you can walk in on grass. Block heels, wedges, flats, or loafers work better than stilettos, which sink into lawns.
Pick one statement piece, such as a bold color, a hat, or a patterned fabric, and keep the rest of the outfit simpler.
avoid: Heavy, dark fabrics like wool or thick denim, which trap heat in the afternoon sun.
Very long or very dragging hems and stiletto heels, which catch on grass and pavers.
Wearing all black or overly formal evening wear unless the invitation specifically asks for it.

faq.q: What should I wear to a garden party in the summer?
faq.a: Choose light, breathable fabrics like cotton, linen, or a light floral print in a comfortable cut. Add sun protection such as a hat or sunglasses, and keep your shoes comfortable for walking on grass.

faq.q: What do men wear to a garden party?
faq.a: A lightweight suit or a linen shirt with chinos works well, with loafers or suede shoes instead of dress shoes. Avoid a full heavy suit unless the invitation calls for a formal dress code. A panama or straw hat is a classic finishing touch.

faq.q: Are hats appropriate at a garden party?
faq.a: Yes, a sun hat or a straw or panama hat is one of the most fitting accessories for a garden party. Choose one that suits the outfit, and take it off indoors or when the host asks.

h1: What to wear to a graduation

intro: For a graduation, smart casual is the safest choice: polished enough for a formal ceremony and photos, comfortable enough for a long, often warm midday event. Aim for clean, well-fitted pieces in solid or subtle colors, and let your shoes and fit do the work of making the outfit look considered.

looks.caption: Charcoal waistcoat and trousers, a white shirt, tan suede shoes.
looks.why: The Classic look pairs a charcoal waistcoat and matching trousers with a crisp white shirt and tan suede shoes. It reads as sharp and celebratory without being stiff, and the neutral palette photographs well against gowns and campus backdrops.

looks.caption: Turquoise floral halter maxi dress under the graduation gown.
looks.why: The Bold look is a turquoise floral halter maxi dress. It stands out in group photos, and the lightweight fabric and open back keep you cool at midday. Because the gown covers most of the dress, it works especially well when you are wearing the gown.

looks.caption: Houndstooth blazer, a black open-collar shirt, wide black trousers.
looks.why: The Relaxed look combines a houndstooth blazer with a black open-collar shirt and wide black trousers. The mix of pattern and black keeps it modern and polished, and the open collar and wide cut make it comfortable for a long day on your feet.

tips: Check the dress code on the invitation or school website; if the ceremony is outdoors or in a gym, lean slightly more casual.
At around 21°C, a light layer such as a blazer or cardigan is enough, since it's easy to remove once you're in the sun.
Choose shoes you can stand in for hours, such as loafers, low block heels, or leather derbies, and break them in beforehand.
Stick to a palette of two to three colors, and avoid anything that clashes with a black or dark gown.
Pay attention to fit at the shoulders and hem, and keep accessories simple: one statement piece like a watch, earrings, or a tie is plenty.
avoid: Overly casual items like sneakers, graphic tees, or distressed denim.
Bright white or very light outfits that may show dust, sweat marks, or wrinkles from sitting in the sun.
Anything you haven't worn before, especially new shoes that might cause blisters on a long day.

faq.q: What should I wear under a graduation gown?
faq.a: Wear whatever you'd wear to the event itself, since the gown covers most of your outfit. Focus on the parts that show, like your neckline, sleeves, and shoes. Keep the layers underneath comfortable, because gowns can trap heat.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear a dress to a graduation?
faq.a: Yes, a dress is a great choice for a graduation. Pick a midi or maxi length in a fabric suited to the temperature, and add a light jacket or cardigan if you want more polish.

faq.q: What should men wear to a graduation?
faq.a: A well-fitted blazer or waistcoat with tailored trousers and a collared shirt works for most graduations. Open-collar or a tie can be dressed up or down depending on the event's formality.

h1: What to wear to a cocktail party

intro: A cocktail party calls for polished, dressed-up clothing that still feels relaxed enough to move around and chat. For most people the safest choice is a fitted or structured outfit in a rich color, finished with clean, elegant shoes. Dress up one notch more than you think you need, then adjust for the venue and the evening's temperature.

looks.caption: Red and navy floral off-shoulder gown, black strappy sandals.
looks.why: The Classic look: a red and navy floral off-shoulder gown with black strappy sandals is a timeless, polished choice that reads as elegant without trying too hard.

looks.why: The Bold look: a cream shawl-collar jacket with flared white trousers and black pointed shoes gives a sharp, tailored statement that works for any gender and stands out in a crowd.

looks.caption: Red satin one-shoulder maxi dress, silver strappy sandals.
looks.why: The Relaxed look: a red satin one-shoulder maxi dress with silver strappy sandals keeps the mood festive and easygoing while still feeling clearly dressy.

tips: Match the dress code: at a 16°C evening event, aim for dressy rather than casual, and wear a blazer, wrap, or cardigan you can add or remove as the room changes temperature.
Choose one statement element, such as a bold color, a striking print, or a tailored jacket, and keep everything else simple.
Pick closed-toe pointed shoes or strappy heels you can stand in for two hours; test them at home first.
Keep jewelry and accessories coordinated: one metal finish, a small clutch or slim bag, and no more than two standout pieces.

Overloading on competing prints, bright colors, and heavy accessories at the same time.

faq.q: What is the dress code for a cocktail party?
faq.a: Cocktail attire usually means dressy but not black-tie: a cocktail dress, a suit, or tailored separates. If the invitation says cocktail attire, dress one level above smart casual.

faq.q: What should a man wear to a cocktail party?
faq.a: A well-fitted suit or a blazer with tailored trousers and a open-collar or fine-knit shirt is a strong choice. Wear leather dress shoes, and skip a tie unless the invitation calls for one.

faq.q: Can I wear a jumpsuit to a cocktail party?
faq.a: Yes. A tailored or silky jumpsuit in a rich color works well for a cocktail party, especially when paired with polished heels or pointed shoes and a structured jacket for cooler evenings.

h1: Comfortable travel day outfits

Airports and planes often run cool, and destinations can be warmer or colder than where you started, so plan for flexibility. Peppi shows three complete outfits for your trip, each checked against the weather where you'll be.

looks.why: The Bold look uses a sky-blue double-breasted blazer over a hot-pink top, with a matching scarf and white trousers. The structured blazer keeps the outfit polished for a long layover or arrival, and the bright color makes you easy to spot in a crowd.

looks.why: The Relaxed look is a white button-up shirt with light-wash jeans and off-white sneakers. It's the lightest option, easy to layer with a jacket or cardigan in your bag, and the sneakers handle long walks through terminals.

tips: Dress for a range of temperatures: wear a base layer you can wear alone, then add a jacket or scarf you can take off and pack.
Choose a jacket with inside pockets so your phone, passport and boarding pass stay within reach.
Wear shoes you've already broken in, and choose slip-on or easy-lace styles if you'll go through security often.
Stick to two or three colors that mix easily, so you can pack fewer pieces and still have options at your destination.
Pick stretch fabrics or relaxed cuts for jeans and trousers, since you'll be sitting for hours. Men and women can both use these fits; for women, a wrap or cardigan adds warmth without bulk.
avoid: Tight waistbands or stiff seams that feel fine standing but uncomfortable after several hours seated.
Heavy outerwear that's hard to take off in a crowded terminal or cabin.
Brand-new shoes or sandals with no support for a day of walking and standing.

faq.q: What is the most comfortable thing to wear on a long flight?
faq.a: Soft, breathable fabrics like cotton, knits and a little stretch in your jeans or trousers work best. Layers let you adjust as the cabin temperature changes.

faq.q: How do I dress for a travel day when the destination weather is different?
faq.a: Dress for your departure temperature and pack one warm or light layer for the other end. A jacket, scarf or cardigan you can carry solves most mismatches.

faq.q: What shoes are best for traveling?
faq.a: Choose shoes with cushioned soles and a secure fit that you can walk in for hours. Loafers, supportive sneakers and slip-on styles are all practical picks for both men and women.

Bring a layer you can add or remove: a trench, light jacket or cardigan handles mornings that warm up fast.
Pick shoes you can walk in, since brunch often means a stroll before or after the table.

Shoes that are new and stiff or that you can't stand in for an hour.

faq.q: What is the dress code for brunch?
faq.a: Brunch is usually smart casual, so you can be relaxed but should look put together. Clean jeans or trousers with a good top, or a simple dress, work for most places. If the venue is upscale, lean toward the Classic look.

faq.q: What should I wear to brunch when it's cold?
faq.a: Layer. A trench, jacket or knit over a simple top and trousers keeps you warm and lets you adjust once you're inside. Choose closed shoes or boots and add a scarf for warmth and color.

h1: What to wear to a concert
title: What to wear to a concert · Peppi
description: Not sure what to wear to a concert? Get three complete outfit ideas for your night, matched to the weather and how dressed up you want to be.
context: Concert night · Evening · 22°C · Formality 3 · Casual
intro: For most concerts, smart casual is the safest choice: comfortable shoes, clothes you can move in, and a layer for when the venue gets cold or sweaty. Aim for an outfit that looks put together without feeling stiff, since you'll likely be standing, dancing, or squeezed into a crowd for hours.

looks.caption: Long black coat over a white tee, pinstriped wide trousers.
looks.why: Classic: a long black coat over a white tee with pinstriped wide trousers. The coat adds polish and warmth for an evening outdoor show, while the tee and relaxed trousers keep it easy to move in.

looks.caption: White jumpsuit with a bold black leaf print, strappy heels.
looks.why: Bold: a white jumpsuit with a black leaf print and strappy heels. One piece does the work, and the print gives you a strong look that stands out in a dim, crowded room.

looks.caption: Tan suede bomber, a white tee, slim blue jeans, white sneakers.
looks.why: Relaxed: a tan suede bomber over a white tee, slim blue jeans, and white sneakers. It's the most practical option for standing all night, and the suede jacket keeps it from looking too casual.

tips: Check the venue type and dress code first: arena and festival crowds usually go casual, while a theater or seated show may call for a bit more polish.
Dress in layers. Venues can be cold near the door and hot once the crowd builds, so a jacket or overshirt you can tie or carry is a good idea.
Prioritize comfortable shoes. Sneakers or low-heeled boots work for standing; save strappy heels for shows where you'll be seated or for a short night.
Stick to darker colors or pieces with some texture if you expect a lot of spilled drinks or dust, and lighter tones if the venue is well lit and you want to show up clearly in photos.
Keep accessories simple: a crossbody bag or small backpack leaves your hands free and keeps your belongings secure in a crowd.
avoid: Brand-new shoes you haven't broken in, since blisters can ruin a long show.
Heavy bags or overstuffed pockets that bang into people and slow you down in the crowd.
Overdressing for a standing-room show, where a formal outfit can feel out of place and get uncomfortable fast.

faq.q: What should I wear to a concert in summer?
faq.a: Choose breathable fabrics like cotton or linen and a loose fit so you stay cool in a crowd. Bring a light layer for the evening, since temperatures often drop after dark, and wear comfortable closed-toe shoes or sneakers.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear jeans to a concert?
faq.a: Yes, jeans are fine for almost any concert, from rock shows to indoor arenas. Pick a pair that's comfortable for standing and dancing, and pair them with a top or jacket that's a step up from everyday wear if you want a more polished look.

faq.q: What do men wear to a concert?
faq.a: Men can go with dark or neutral jeans or trousers, a tee or button-down, and sneakers or boots, plus a jacket or overshirt for layering. The same principles apply as for any concert: comfort first, a polished top half, and shoes you can stand in for hours.

Layer in thin pieces, like a knit under a coat, rather than one bulky item, so you can adjust as you move between cold streets and heated rooms.
Choose shoes you can walk in all day. Boots with a bit of grip are the safest choice for cold, possibly wet pavement.
Keep the palette tight: one or two strong colors with neutrals, such as cream, black or denim, so the outfit looks deliberate.
Add one detail that adds warmth or interest, like a beret, a scarf, gloves or a bag in a contrast color.
avoid: Thin fabrics that look nice but do not block wind, such as unlined linen or a light jacket with no insulation.
Shoes with smooth soles or open toes, which get slippery and cold quickly in winter.
Too many competing patterns or colors, which can make a cold-weather layered look feel busy.

faq.q: What should I wear for a winter day in the city?
faq.a: Wear a warm, structured coat over a knit or turtleneck, with comfortable trousers or a dress and boots with grip. Layer so you can adjust indoors and outdoors.

faq.q: How do I stay warm in the city in winter without looking bulky?
faq.a: Use thin, warm layers like a fine-knit turtleneck under a well-fitted coat. Choose a coat with some structure so it looks tailored rather than puffy, and add a scarf or hat for extra warmth at the neck and head.

faq.q: What shoes are best for walking around the city in winter?
faq.a: Boots with a sturdy, grippy sole and a comfortable fit are the best choice. Knee-high boots work well with trousers or a dress, but make sure you can walk comfortably in them for hours.
